clue.text: A bit of third degree from Little Tom's lot

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so his possession is Thumb's
a lot is a group of people, a crew

explanation.surface: Some rough questioning delivered by a small boy's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The third degree is harsh interrogation, sometimes with torture; Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval torture device that crushed the fingers is a literal instrument of brutal interrogation.

clue.text: Husky animal by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to take a word as heard, not as written

parts.note: a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: A sled dog that sounds like some other beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, a synonym.

clue.text: Otto (amateur) overturned the warlike Indian

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned means the joined pieces read upwards, last letter first

parts.note: otto is another name for attar, the perfume oil of roses
a ham is an amateur, as in a radio ham

explanation.surface: A hobbyist called Otto topples a fierce warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns ATTARHAM round to give the answer. Otto looks like a man's name but is the rose oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maratha people of western India were renowned as a fighting race; this is an old spelling.

clue.text: Appears to accept poetry of decent quality

indicators.note: one word taking in another, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: appears means seems
lines are verses of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone appears willing to take on verse of respectable standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemliness is propriety, behaviour that is proper and becoming.

clue.text: Firm purpose to settle

explanation.surface: A determination to sort things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm purpose is a determination, a noun sense; to settle a dispute or problem is a verb sense.

clue.text: Look out for pottery

explanation.surface: A warning to watch the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ware is an old verb meaning beware or watch out, and the noun means manufactured ceramics, as in earthenware.

clue.text: Being a stripper she gets a call

parts.note: taken as written
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A striptease artist receives a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a dancer but someone clipping the fleece off sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping wool from sheep strips them of their fleece.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one drink as a starter

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an orator is a speaker
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A public speaker downs a drink before kicking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who starts something off is its creator or founder.

clue.text: Gold hammer-thrower as 8

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Thor, the Norse god of thunder, hurls his hammer

explanation.surface: An athlete in the hammer event wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, someone who starts things off; the hammer-thrower is not an athlete but the Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer or creator of something is its originator.

clue.text: Such a waste! No way to get over it

definitions.text: Such a waste! No way to get over it

parts.words: Such a waste! No way to get over it
parts.note: a waste here is a wilderness, and having no track across it describes it exactly

explanation.surface: A lament over squandered resources that one cannot recover from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' and 'get over it' suggest regret, but this is a barren expanse with no track across.
explanation.definitionFit: Trackless land has no route through it.

clue.text: Beetle's about — dash!

parts.note: over can mean concerning or about, as in a row over money
hang and dash are both mild oaths, as in hang it or dash it

explanation.surface: An exclamation of irritation about an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a verb here: to project, as beetling brows jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to jut out, which is what a projecting ledge does.

clue.text: Vote in group for canonical office at noon …

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a set is a group
an X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A committee votes on a church service held at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the monastic hours, the sixth hour's prayer service falls at midday.

clue.text: A gullible type goes after visionary material

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so it is placed second

parts.note: a seer is a visionary prophet
a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A fool chases after fabric seen in a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A puckered striped cotton or linen fabric is a type of cloth.

clue.text: … in calling for prayer

parts.note: a calling is a vocation

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a summons to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis continues the previous clue's sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling on God in a church service is an act of prayer.

clue.text: Terribly lined, Clare is a neglected person

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Clare, badly wrinkled, is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' signals rearranging the letters of LINED and CLARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine kept in the kitchen by her stepsisters gives her name to anyone overlooked.

clue.text: Tried to be like Bacon

explanation.surface: An attempt to emulate the philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was famous for his Essays, so to be like him is to have written essays.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it; Bacon was the great Elizabethan essayist.

clue.text: Animal hunted with a net perhaps seen to become sluggish

parts.note: a stag is hunted as game

indicators.note: perhaps marks the words a net as only one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Caught in a net, a hunted beast slows down.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale water that stops flowing goes still, so a person or economy can become inactive too.

clue.text: One thing's not clear discernment needed

definitions.text: One thing's not clear discernment needed

parts.words: One thing's not clear discernment needed
parts.note: when something is murky one needs the perceptive faculty of seeing into it

explanation.surface: A puzzling matter needs good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Penetrating understanding is the ability to see into a situation.

clue.text: Impressions of stamps

explanation.surface: Marks left by a rubber stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressions are marks pressed into a surface, a noun; to stamp a mark is a verb.

clue.text: One who is contemptuous of an S-bend?

parts.note: taken as the letter S
a bend in a road is a corner

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a winding road.
explanation.walkthrough: An S-bend is a road curve shaped like the letter, so an S-corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scorns others treats them with disdain.

clue.text: Vesta's wild area for larkspur

indicators.note: wild letters run free and take a new order

parts.note: the name with its letter s is the fodder
an acre is a measure of area

explanation.surface: The goddess Vesta's untamed land, where a flower grows.
explanation.definitionFit: This poisonous plant is a species of delphinium, the larkspur family.

clue.text: A nut tree's golden fruit

parts.note: the nursery rhyme I Had a Little Nut Tree says it bore nothing but a silver nutmeg and a golden fruit

explanation.surface: Gilded produce from a hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: A nut tree bears no other fruit, but in the English nursery rhyme its only crops were a silver nutmeg and this golden fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the fruit is a golden one of the orchard kind.

clue.text: Financial backer a girl

parts.note: an angel is an investor who backs a theatre show

explanation.surface: A girl who funds a venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name.

clue.text: Vermilion for Roman Poet's Pub

parts.note: Helvius Cinna was a Roman poet, killed by the mob in Julius Caesar
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A red paint chosen for a tavern named after a classical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury sulphide ore gives a bright red pigment of that shade.

clue.text: A bit of a blow for the head reader

definitions.text: A bit of a blow for the head reader

parts.words: A bit of a blow for the head reader
parts.note: a knock leaves a swelling, and phrenologists read character from the swellings of the skull

explanation.surface: A setback for the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The head reader is a phrenologist, who claimed to read character from the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling from a knock is also a lump on the skull read by a phrenologist.

clue.text: Not one who yearns — not any more

parts.note: no means not, as in no better
a person who longs for something is a longer

explanation.surface: Someone stops pining.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now.

clue.text: Good reputation to consider

explanation.surface: A fine name worth thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, a noun; to esteem is to deem or regard, a verb.

clue.text: Anna's Paris, strangely poetic

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd new order

parts.note: the name with its letter s is the fodder

explanation.surface: Anna's view of Paris is oddly lyrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Parnassus was sacred to the Muses, so the adjective describes poetry.
